(a) Three-dimensional view illustrating the physical boundaries, including the inlet (A), outlets (B–D), object surface (E), and periodic side-walls (F,G). (b) 2D side view showing characteristic dimensions relative to theobject thicknessDD. Note that black lines have no physical implications but indicate regions used for mesh refinement.

Figure 7:Two-dimensional (x​yxy-)plane of the computational mesh. The full three-dimensional domain is a 30-layer extrusion in thezzdirection. (a) Full domain. (b) Zoomed-in view of the geometric object.

Figure 8:Comparison between present simulations (solid black markers) and validation data from the literature (open and hatched markers) for (a) Strouhal number, (b) drag coefficient, and (c) recirculation length. Validation data are taken at discrete Reynolds numbers from the following sources: Re=1000(Jiang and Cheng, 2017); Re=1783(Bai and Alam, 2018); Re=2000 (hatched)(Sharma and Dutta, 2022)and (open)(Brun et al., 2008); Re=3000(Cimarelli et al., 2018); Re=3900(Lehmkuhl et al., 2013).

Figure 15:Comparison between the present study (top row) andCimarelli et al. (2018)(bottom row) of the mean flow field above the rectangular surface. Streamlines of the mean velocity field are shown in (a), and the mean pressure field in (b). In (a), green lines indicate theprimary vortex, red lines thesecondary vortex, and black lines thewake vortex.
